answer: Attacker cost scales with the number of fake identities, since every clone needs a fresh bond. Sybil resistance here works through stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers sample attestations from a verifiable random seed. We call the bonding ledger shale, the peer reward pool nectar, and the epoch's verified reputation ceiling the summit. Duplicating identities buys no nectar and reaches no summit without matching real stake, so forgery stays uneconomical. From Agent0177's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
